title: A third, a receipt, and a nine-hundred-dollar part
summary: Pew Research Center estimates that thirty-five percent of English-language web pages published since ChatGPT's launch show signs of machine authorship — and the domain breakdown, not the headline, is what makes the number credible. Then StateM claims ninety-five point three percent on Terminal-Bench 2.1 without touching a model weight, for fifteen dollars against five hundred seventy-four, and the half-point held-out result that complicates it. Plus the nine-hundred-ninety-nine-dollar Nvidia module Ukraine pulled out of a Russian cruise missile, which was never on any export control list.

topics: Pew Research Center analysis of machine authorship on the English-language web: close to half a million pages collected over five years, a random sample of 10,000 pages from July 2026 run through the Pangram detector; ~10% of the whole sample and 35% of pages published after ChatGPT's November 2022 launch show significant signs of AI authorship; .com roughly 10x the rate of .edu/.gov (both ~1%), .org at 4.6%; Pew's own caveat that detectors can misclassify but the data is likely at least directionally correct — with the domain spread read on air as structure that a flat false-positive rate would not produce, and provenance identified as the axis retrieval stacks track least

StateM (Ziheng Qin, Yaxin Lu, Zhangyang Atlas Wang, Kai Wang; posted 2026-08-18, 431 HF upvotes): agent-native runtime built on durable states, phase-local context, checked transitions, recoverable runbooks and versioned procedural practices, with model weights frozen. Terminal-Bench 2.1: GPT-5.5 xhigh 83.1 to 92.1; GPT-5.6 Sol xhigh 95.3% raw across 445 trials, succeeding on all 89 tasks at least once; frozen profile lifts GPT-5.6 Luna 76.7 to 85.4, above the 84.9 Sol xhigh reference; under $38 of adaptation lifts DeepSeek-V4-Flash 82.7 to 88.1; final-score API usage ~$15 vs $574.68 for the GPT reference, total DeepSeek spend $52.22. BusinessBench held-out gains of only 0.55 macro / 1.34 micro points, with two mechanism-matched families improving 10.04 — the authors' own line that concrete rules generalize when tasks share execution structure

Ukraine's Defence Intelligence (announced 2026-08-12) recovered an Nvidia Jetson Orin NX 16GB module and an electro-optical camera from an S-71M 'Monokrom' cruise missile, saying the component indicates possible use of AI technology; the module lists at $999, does ~100 TOPS INT8 and draws 10-25W, and sits below the training-class threshold US export controls are drawn at; Nvidia's statement that used Jetsons move through many resale channels and it cannot track products after sale; GUR reports 5,816 foreign-made components identified across 202 types of Russian weapons systems, with no published split between evaded controls and uncontrolled parts

threads.name: AI sovereignty and open weights
threads.status: The thread's export-control leg moved to a category the rules never covered: Ukraine's Defence Intelligence recovered a $999 Nvidia Jetson Orin NX from an S-71M cruise missile, a part deliberately below the training-class threshold the controls are drawn at, with Nvidia stating it cannot track resold units.
threads.arc: From arguments about whether frontier weights and data-center GPUs should be restricted, to a demonstration that the consequential hardware in this instance was a commodity edge module nobody proposed restricting.

dives.story: Pew's estimate that 35% of post-ChatGPT web pages show signs of machine authorship
dives.why_it_matters: Anyone building search, retrieval, or a training corpus is now sourcing from a web whose provenance they cannot see, and this is the first large-sample estimate of how much of it that affects.

dives.story: StateM: 95.3% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 by scaling the harness instead of the model
dives.why_it_matters: Teams choosing between a more expensive model and better scaffolding now have a concrete cost comparison and a concrete design to copy — and a held-out number that says how far it actually transfers.

dives.story: A $999 Nvidia Jetson module recovered from a Russian cruise missile
dives.why_it_matters: Everyone shipping or regulating edge AI hardware has a worked example of why controls drawn at the top of the performance curve miss the class of part that is cheap, ubiquitous, and good enough.

concepts_taught: harness scaling as a design: durable states, phase-local context, code-checked phase transitions, recoverable runbooks, and versioned procedural practices — improving the execution system around an agent with model weights frozen

why a domain-type breakdown is evidence about detector reliability: a flat false-positive rate would produce a flat rate across .com/.org/.edu/.gov, so a ten-to-one spread is structure rather than noise
why export controls drawn at the top of the performance curve fail on commodity edge inference hardware: the historical regime depended on the controlled part being rare, expensive, and countable
